title: Best Window of Size k

concept.title: A window that slides
body: The sum of `k` consecutive elements (a **window**) is not recomputed from scratch when the window moves one step to the right. The new window loses its first element and gains one new element, so the sum changes by `a[i] - a[i - k]`.

body.code:
window = sum(a[:k])
best = window
for i in range(k, n):
    window += a[i] - a[i - k]
    best = max(best, window)

body: That makes the work O(n) instead of O(n * k). Sliding windows are used whenever the answer is about a block of consecutive elements.

statement: Given an array of `n` integers (negative numbers are possible) and a number `k`, find the largest sum of `k` consecutive elements.

examples.note: The windows have sums 4, 7, 8 and 5, so the answer is 8 (5 4 -1).

hints: Compute the sum of the first window directly.
When the window moves, subtract the element that leaves and add the element that enters.

explanation: Each step of the window changes the sum by one added and one removed element, so every window sum is found in O(1).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

window = sum(a[:k])
best = window
for i in range(k, n):
    window += a[i] - a[i - k]
    best = max(best, window)
print(best)
